title: Substitution
summary: Learn how to replace letters with numbers carefully, including negatives, brackets, powers and formulae.

blocks.text: Substitution means putting a number into a formula or expression in place of a letter

blocks.title: Example 1: Find the value of 4a + b when a = 5 and b = 3

steps.body:
In this question we are going to change a into 5 and b into 3

We cannot write 45 + 3 because 4b means 4 times b  
We can instead use brackets to substitute the numbers into the expression:  
4(5) + (3)

4(5) means 4 × 5  
4 × 5 = 20

We now have: 20 + 3  
20 + 3 = 23

blocks.title: Example 2: Find the value of 4a - 3b when a = 7 and b = 2

steps.body:
This time we are going to change a into 7 and b into 2

We can use brackets to substitute the numbers into the expression:  
4(7) - 3(2)

4(7) means 4 × 7  
4 × 7 = 28

3(2) means 3 × 2  
3 × 2 = 6

We now have: 28 - 6  
28 - 6 = 22

items.explanation: Substitute the values and multiply first: $3(4)+2(7)=12+14=26$.
Substitution gives $5(6)-4(2)=30-8=22$. The terms are subtracted, not added.

blocks.title: Example 3: Find the value of 4a² - 3b when a = 3 and b = 7

steps.body:
4(3)² - 3(7)

The order of operations tells us that the first step is to square the 3

3² = 9

We now have: 4(9) - 3(7)

4 × 9 = 36  
3 × 7 = 21

36 - 21 = 15

blocks.title: Example 4: Find the value of 5a² - ab when a = -3 and b = -2

steps.body:
5(-3)² - (-3)(-2)

The order of operations tells us that the first step is to square the negative 3

A negative times a negative is a positive  
(-3)² = (-3) × (-3) = 9

We now have: 5(9) - (-3)(-2)

5 × 9 = 45  
\-3 × -2 = 6

45 - 6 = 39

items.explanation: Use brackets around the negative value: $(-4)^2-2(3)(2)=16-12=4$. Squaring a negative number gives a positive result.

blocks.title: Example 5: Find the value of 5ab - bc when a = 3, b = -2 and c = 4

steps.body:
5(3)(-2) - (-2)(4)

We can do the multiplication of 5 × 3 × -2 in any order  
5 × 3 = 15  
15 × -2 = -30 A positive times a negative is a negative

\-2 × 4 = -8

We now have: -30 - -8

When we take away a negative we go up the number line -30 - - 8 = -30 + 8 = -22

items.explanation: Substitute using brackets: $4(-3)-2(-5)=-12-(-10)=-12+10=-2$. Subtracting a negative is the same as adding.

items.prompt: A formula is $R=\frac{p^2-q^2}{2r}$. Find $R$ when $p=7$, $q=3$ and $r=5$.
items.explanation: Substitute into the numerator and denominator: $R=\frac{7^2-3^2}{2(5)}=\frac{49-9}{10}=\frac{40}{10}=4$.
Substitute all three values: $2(3)(-2)+(-2)(4)=-12-8=-20$. Both products are negative.
Substitute $k=5$ and evaluate the bracket first: $3(5+2)-4=3(7)-4=21-4=17$.
